title: Waymo in Dallas
author: xnx
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Starting today, anyone in Dallas can download the Waymo app and hail a fully autonomous ride. Since opening our service in February, we’ve welcomed nearly 150,000 riders in Dallas from our interest list to experience the safety, reliability, and magic of Waymo, and now we’re offering our service to everyone.We’ve proudly helped Dallasites run errands, commute to work, and celebrate nights out with friends. Now, we’re going a step further to unlock a new way for tourists and other visitors to get around the city. We continue fully autonomous testing at Dallas Love Field Airport terminals and look forward to serving travelers there soon. And to get there efficiently, we’ll soon begin fully autonomous testing on Dallas freeways, which is the final step before offering these routes to public riders.The Dallas community has embraced Waymo as a vital resource for expanding accessible and reliable transportation options across the region. Chris Justl, CEO, Epilepsy Foundation Texas, shared, "Waymo autonomous vehicles are not just the future—they’re a transformational step forward for the epilepsy community and anyone living with medical conditions that limit their ability to drive, creating a new pathway to safe, independent travel. At Epilepsy Foundation Texas, we’re proud to partner with Waymo to help bring this future to life across Texas.”Rolling with Waymo in Dallas has never been easier. Simply download the Waymo app and ride today!

comments.author: eagleinparadise
comments.textRawHtml:
As someone who works in commercial real estate, involved in about $300M of housing development, some of it affordable, i will say without any doubt that driverless cars are a very effective affordable housing policy that is not being considered or discussed by anyone.

Any public dollar that gets contributed to housing, basically adds a 50% cost factor and assume whatever it is used for will take 2-3x as long to deliver anything you can live in.

So instead, Cities should lease Waymos (or other brands), and provide these vehicles for use by affordable tenants in properties with limited parking.

Building housing with no parking is not feasible for 95% of deals. You simply won't get financing or you'll end up handing the keys back to the lender and bankrupt on the deal. Instead, if you could hand to your investors and lender an agreement which provides a car for every 3 units, that tenants have first priority to use for free (or an amount subsidized per month) up to reasonable limits, then you'd address the concern "where are people going to park and how to get to work?".

it's way more efficient than building $100 billion in transit that will take 200 years to build.

What's it cost per year to lease? $30k? That car can be full time serving 4-10 units daily? The cars can be rented to the public on off hours to offset their operating cost.

It's a lot more cost efficient and can be done TODAY, not 5 years after complicated LIHTC financing with 4 layers of other public funding, 3 years of approvals, and 2 years of construction.
comments.textZhHtml:
作为从事商业房地产工作的人，参与了约 3 亿美元的住房开发，其中一些是经济适用房，我毫无疑问地说，无人驾驶汽车是一项非常有效的经济适用房政策，但没有被任何人考虑或讨论过。

任何用于住房的公共资金基本上都会增加 50% 的成本因素，并假设无论它用于什么，都需要 2-3 倍的时间才能交付你可以居住的任何东西。

所以相反，城市应该租赁 Waymos（或其他品牌），并提供这些车辆，供停车位有限的房产中负担得起的租户使用。

对于 95% 的交易来说，建造没有停车位的住房是不可行的。你根本无法获得融资，或者最终将钥匙交还给贷方并在交易中破产。相反，如果您可以向投资者和贷方提供一份协议，每 3 个单位提供一辆汽车，并且租户在合理限度内拥有优先免费使用（或每月补贴金额）的权利，那么您就可以解决“人们在哪里停车以及如何上班？”的问题。

这比建造 1000 亿美元、需要 200 年才能建成的交通运输系统要高效得多。

每辆汽车的成本是多少。租赁年份？ 3万美元？那辆车每天可以全职服务4-10辆吗？这些汽车可以在下班时间向公众出租，以抵消其运营成本。

这更具成本效益，并且可以在今天完成，而不是在复杂的 LIHTC 融资（包括 4 层其他公共资金）、3 年的审批和 2 年的建设之后 5 年后完成。

children.author: Grombobulous
children.textRawHtml:
With respect to you as a person and your ideas presented, this is one of the most car-brained posts I've ever read.

> it's way more efficient than building $100 billion in transit that will take 200 years to build.

What is efficient about a $13 highway widening project in Houston or the $24 billion (inflation-adjusted) and 15 years it cost to bury a highway in Boston? (It's not even much of a new highway, it's just underground now!)

I don't think the average person realizes how little typical non-New York states spend on transit. Ohio's ratio on highways:public transit spending is approximately 8:1, and that includes federal public transit money. Oh yeah, and Ohio outspends all its bordering neighbors per-capita.

I am here to tell you about this cutting-edge science-fiction technology that is cheap, efficient, highly flexible, and requires almost zero infrastructure investment: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus

As a bonus, instead of funneling public money out of state to Waymo who then dumps into cars manufactured by Zeekr in China, the city bus actually employs local people!

It's so fascinating that Arlington, Texas, a city with over 300,000 people in it, hasn't yet been able to master the deep intricacies and mystical technology of the bus.

I've also noticed that you are talking about the impacts of transit and vehicles on real estate prices, e.g., a lack or excess of parking spaces. I think you can do something similar the other way around and investigate the real estate impact of permanent rapid transit stations being built. That paradigm is how Japan funds its entire public transit system as a profitable enterprise: allow the rail company to own and develop real estate in close proximity to the stations.
children.textZhHtml:
就您个人以及您所提出的想法而言，这是我读过的最有汽车头脑的帖子之一。

>这比花费 200 年建造 1000 亿美元的交通设施要高效得多。

休斯敦 13 美元的高速公路拓宽项目或 240 亿美元（经通货膨胀调整）和 15 年时间埋藏一条高速公路的效率如何？波士顿？ （它甚至算不上一条新高速公路，现在只是在地下！）

我认为普通人没有意识到典型的非纽约州在交通上的支出有多么少。俄亥俄州的高速公路与公共交通支出之比约为 8:1，其中包括联邦公共交通资金。哦，是的，俄亥俄州的人均支出超过了所有毗邻邻国。

我来这里是为了向您介绍这种尖端的科幻技术，它廉价、高效、高度灵活，并且几乎需要零基础设施投资：https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus

作为奖励，不要将公共资金从该州转移到 Waymo，然后再投入到 Zeekr 制造的汽车中在中国，城市公交车居然雇用当地人！

令人着迷的是，德克萨斯州阿灵顿这个拥有超过30万人口的城市还无法掌握公交车的深奥和神秘技术。

我还注意到您在谈论交通和车辆对房地产价格的影响，例如停车位的缺乏或过剩。我认为你可以反过来做类似的事情，调查正在建设的永久性快速交通站对房地产的影响。这种模式就是日本如何为其整个公共交通系统提供资金作为盈利企业：允许铁路公司拥有和开发靠近车站的房地产。

children.author: missedthecue
children.textRawHtml: the simple fact of the matter is the Waymo is a better public transport solution for Dallas than the bus. The bus doesn't work very well in endless cul-de-sac suburbia, and that's what the Dallas/Fort Worth area (and indeed most of America) is. Like, you have to understand that most of Dallas isn't even commuting into downtown Dallas every day to work. They are just commuting to other suburbs and then back to their suburb. If your public transport solution is step 1. nuke the place and start over, it's not really a solution.
children.textZhHtml: 事实很简单，对于达拉斯来说，Waymo 是比公交车更好的公共交通解决方案。公交车在无边无际的死胡同郊区不太好用，达拉斯/沃斯堡地区（实际上是美国大部分地区）就是这样。就像，你必须明白，达拉斯的大部分人甚至不是每天都通勤到达拉斯市中心上班。他们只是通勤到其他郊区，然后再返回自己的郊区。如果您的公共交通解决方案是第一步：用核武器攻击该地方并重新开始，那么这并不是一个真正的解决方案。

children.author: yreg
children.textRawHtml:
Why is a bus not fit for endless culdesac suburbia where people are commuting between the suburbs instead of to the downtown?

I really don't get it. Pretty much everywhere outside of US buses work no matter the city layout. Just add some stops and run some buses.
children.textZhHtml:
为什么公交车不适合无尽的死胡同郊区，人们在郊区之间通勤而不是去市中心？

我真的不明白。无论城市布局如何，美国以外的几乎所有地方都可以使用公交车。只需添加一些站点并运行一些公交车即可。

children.author: missedthecue
children.textRawHtml:
because you can't fill the buses!

1. Cul-de-sacs and surburbia lack through-streets. So it forces heavy long buses to navigate winding narrow loops. This makes your routing complex and slow.

2. When commuters travel suburb-to-suburb instead of hub-and-spoke downtown, origin-destination pairs are too scattered to support fixed routes with meaningful frequency.

3. Low passenger volume per mile makes fixed-route bus operations financially unsustainable.

4. Disconnected street networks and long setbacks force residents to drive just to reach a bus stop. Like seriously pull up google maps. There are a million suburbs in the greater DFW area where you need to walk 15 minutes just to get out of your neighborhood to the nearest main road where a bus stop would be placed. When it's a thirty minute round trip of walking, (not to mention what the walking situation looks like at your destination), and you throw in stopping at every bus stop on the route, every commute takes several hours instead of 20-30 minutes driving.
children.textZhHtml:
因为你无法填满公交车！

1.死胡同和郊区缺乏直通街道。因此，它迫使重型长巴士在蜿蜒狭窄的环路中行驶。这使得您的路由变得复杂且缓慢。

2.当通勤者从郊区到郊区而不是中心辐射型市中心出行时，出发地-目的地对过于分散，无法支持具有有意义的频率的固定路线。

3.每英里客运量低使得固定路线巴士运营在经济上难以为继。

4.断开的街道网络和漫长的挫折迫使居民开车才能到达公交车站。就像认真地打开谷歌地图一样。那里DFW 地区有 100 万个郊区，您需要步行 15 分钟才能走出您的社区，到达最近设有公交车站的主干道。如果步行往返 30 分钟（更不用说目的地的步行情况了），并且您在路线上的每个公交车站都停下来，那么每次通勤都需要几个小时，而不是 20-30 分钟的车程。

children.author: yreg
children.textRawHtml:
1. I promise you that a bus can get through winding narrow loops just fine. All medieval old towns are like that.

2. You either create loops or hubs where people transfer. The hub can be just a regular bus stop where lines meet.

3. Looking up the density of Dallas suburbs I can tell you that buses can work well in far less dense places.

4. The math doesn't add up, if you can get somewhere by car in 20 - 30mins driving then even with 15 minute walk on either side the bus will take you there in less than 'hours'. And walking 15 minutes to the bus stop is not the end of the world. There would also be plenty of people living/working closer to the stop.

From your original comment I got the idea that you think buses need to be these massive heavy vehicles, but that's not really the case either. I've been to places where the public transport was operated by microvans with as low as 12 seats. I don't think they were actually much bigger than american pickups. But I think a regular bus would work alright.
children.textZhHtml:
1. 我向你保证，公共汽车可以顺利通过蜿蜒的狭窄环路。所有中世纪的老城都是这样。

2. 您可以创建人们转移的环路或枢纽。该枢纽可以只是线路交汇的常规巴士站。

3. 查看达拉斯郊区的密度 我可以告诉你，公交车在人口密度低得多的地方也能很好地运行。

4. 数学上说不通，如果您可以在 20 - 30 分钟内驾车到达某个地方，那么即使在两侧步行 15 分钟，巴士也会在不到“小时”的时间内带您到达那里。步行 15 分钟到公交车站并不是世界末日。还有很多人在车站附近生活/工作。

从您最初的评论中，我了解到您认为公共汽车需要是这些大型重型车辆，但事实也并非如此。我去过一些公共交通由低至 12 个座位的微型货车运营的地方。我认为它们实际上并不比美国皮卡大多少。但我认为普通巴士就可以了。

children.author: servo_sausage
children.textRawHtml:
What happens, is your underserved bus has to increase stops per loop for viability.

You have areas where leaving the cul-de-sac zone takes 15-20 minutes on foot; so you need a stop or two in the zone.

Now you have a short walk to the stop; but if you want this to be a viable alternative, you need some frequency of service.

And that means that the routs need to be active across the whole week, not just the hypothetical peak (otherwise everyone needs a car anyway).

So how do you actually get a high average number of riders per bus? More stops?

But if each stop needs to go in and out of a cul-de-sac, the travel time goes up.

Eventually people stop tolerating the extra time, and get cars.

So you end up with a case of empty busses running... Seems much worse than a waymo.
children.textZhHtml:
所发生的情况是，您的服务不足的巴士必须增加每个环路的停靠站才能生存。

在某些区域，离开死胡同区需要步行 15 至 20 分钟；所以你需要在该区域停留一两站。

现在您只需步行一小段路即可到达车站；但如果您希望这是一个可行的替代方案，则需要一定的服务频率。

这意味着路线需要在整个星期都活跃，而不仅仅是假设的高峰期（否则每个人都需要一辆车）。

那么，如何才能让每辆公交车的平均乘客人数达到较高水平呢？更多站点？

但如果每个站点都需要进出死胡同，则旅行时间就会增加。

最终人们不再忍受额外的时间，转而购买汽车。

所以你最终会遇到空巴士运行的情况……看起来比 Waymo 糟糕得多。

children.author: JKCalhoun
children.textRawHtml:
"You have areas where leaving the cul-de-sac zone takes 15-20 minutes on foot…"

Holy shit, you have to walk a mile from a cul-de-sac just to get to a street with an intersection?

Who the hell designed these streets? (I guess Big Auto?)
children.textZhHtml:
“有些地区离开死胡同区需要步行 15 至 20 分钟……”

天哪，你必须走路 一英里 从死胡同只是为了到达有十字路口的街道？

这些街道到底是谁设计的？ （我猜是大汽车？）

children.author: servo_sausage
children.textRawHtml:
Chicken and egg problem. If you start with the assumption that you have a car, they are pretty great. Quiet, no through traffic and can become neighbourly, potentially large blocks. Somewhere to park your car...

Basically trying to retrofit busses to a development built around cars is stupid.
children.textZhHtml:
先有鸡还是先有蛋的问题。如果你从假设你有一辆车开始，它们就非常棒了。安静，没有交通，可以成为邻近的潜在大街区。把车停在某个地方......

基本上，试图将公共汽车改装成围绕汽车建造的开发项目是愚蠢的。

children.author: xnx
children.textRawHtml:
> I've been to places where the public transport was operated by microvans with as low as 12 seats.

Right-sizing the vehicle is smart. Why not also allow 4 person buses that run on demand to and from any point?
children.textZhHtml:
> 我去过公共交通由低至 12 个座位的微型货车运营的地方。

正确调整车辆尺寸是明智之举。为什么不允许 4 人巴士按需运行往返于任何地点？

children.author: bluGill
children.textRawHtml:
Microvans exist. However they are not cost effective. Drivers are expensive and they don't get much better fuel economy than a bus that holds several times the number of passengers. Waymo changes the driver costs but not the other costs of running transit. Worse for the van, it holds few people so you dare not let it get popular because it can't handle a random surge of just two families trying to go somewhere at the same time. Your 4 person bus cannot handle my family of five, which is only slightly above average, there are bigger families in every neighborhood.

A larger bus is needed for useful transit.
children.textZhHtml:
微型货车是存在的。然而，它们并不具有成本效益。司机的费用很高，而且他们的燃油经济性并不比载客数倍的公共汽车好多少。 Waymo 改变了司机成本，但没有改变其他交通运输成本。 对于面包车来说更糟糕的是，它载的人很少，所以你不敢让它受欢迎，因为它无法应对两个家庭同时试图去某个地方的随机激增。你们的 4 人巴士无法容纳我的五口之家，这只是略高于平均水平，每个社区都有更大的家庭。

需要一辆更大的巴士才能提供有用的交通。

children.author: yreg
children.textRawHtml:
Sure, but the Dallas residents still don't have the autonomous on-demand bus while they could have had a normal bus decades ago.

And I doubt that 4 or 12 is the ideal bus size in that place.
children.textZhHtml:
当然，但是达拉斯居民仍然没有自动按需巴士，而几十年前他们就可以拥有普通巴士。

而且我怀疑 4 或 12 辆是那个地方理想的巴士尺寸。

children.author: birdman3131
children.textRawHtml:
I can't say for a properly designed system but I can get anywhere in my city (~90k population / ~0.25m metro) in 15 minutes via car. (Some days traffic effects a bit.)

Many bus stops are up to 1:45 away.

Can and implemented are often worlds apart.

A 12 seater is not a microvan. That is in full size van territory.
children.textZhHtml:
我不能说系统设计得当，但我可以在 15 分钟内驾车到达我所在城市的任何地方（约 9 万人/约 0.25 m 地铁）。 （有时交通会受到一点影响。）

许多巴士站距离酒店最晚 1 点 45 分。

可以和实施往往是天壤之别。

12 座不是微型货车。这是全尺寸货车领域。

children.author: ricardobayes
children.textRawHtml: It works in some countries with a low gini coefficient. In places like Germany or Spain people use public transport because everyone, broadly speaking, is in a very similar socioeconomic status. In some other countries, the wealth inequality is much higher, and people with a higher economic standing don't want to share space with crackheads or mentally ill (a direct consequence of not having access to cheap or free mental health). Some societies are set up in a way that public transport can work, and others don't, it's just the way it is.
children.textZhHtml: 它适用于一些基尼系数较低的国家。在德国或西班牙等地，人们使用公共交通工具，因为一般来说，每个人都处于非常相似的社会经济地位。在其他一些国家，财富不平等程度要高得多，经济地位较高的人不想与瘾君子或精神病患者共享空间（这是无法获得廉价或免费心理健康的直接后果）。有些社会的建立方式是公共交通可以运行，而另一些社会则不然，事情就是这样。

children.author: alooPotato
children.textRawHtml: Just scale your small bus further down and you get a cybercab/waymo. It gets full easily but its routes are fully customizable and you never have to change lines and it runs at all hours with no wait. Ohh and its actually way cheaper to run per passenger mile. IMO shared, electric, autonomous AVs are the best solution for mass transit for 90% of the routes
children.textZhHtml: 只需将您的小型巴士进一步缩小，您就可以得到一辆 Cyber​​cab/waymo。它很容易就满了，但它的路线是完全可定制的，你永远不需要换线，而且它全天候运行，无需等待。哦，实际上每乘客英里的运行成本要便宜得多。 IMO 共享、电动、自动驾驶 AV 是 90% 路线的公共交通的最佳解决方案

children.author: galangalalgol
children.textRawHtml: Lots of single user "busses" cause dramatically lower road wear and microplastics than a many user bus. Those scale with axle weight to the third and fourth powers respectively.
children.textZhHtml: 大量单用户“公交车”比多用户公交车显着降低道路磨损和微塑料。它们分别与轴重的三次方和四次方成比例。

children.author: mnahkies
children.textRawHtml:
Why not both? Driver-less (or even just with drivers) mini buses, without fixed stops and dynamic routes/stops based on demand.

I guess you don't want to stop more times than needed, so maybe you'd want to cluster the demand somehow into "virtual stops", and you may lack some amenities like shelters.. so maybe the traditional bus route is good enough. Though it feels like it's ripe for optimisation (you know the classic no buses come for 30min then 3 arrive at once, or these buses are all full whilst others are roaming empty)
children.textZhHtml:
为什么不两者都选呢？无人驾驶（甚至只有司机）的小型巴士，没有固定站点和基于需求的动态路线/站点。

我想您不想停车超过需要的次数，所以也许您想以某种方式将需求集中到“虚拟站点”中，并且您可能缺乏一些设施，例如庇护所......所以也许传统的巴士路线已经足够好了。虽然感觉优化的时机已经成熟（你知道经典的情况是 30 分钟内没有公交车来，然后 3 辆同时到达，或者这些公交车都满了，而其他公交车却空着）

children.author: infecto
children.textRawHtml: Why would you think it works? Let’s say you have a community of 100 people in Dallas. That neighborhood is going to be commuting in all sorts of directions, sure you might be able to transport some groups going the same direction but there is a complete lack of central offices so how does the last mile work? Lots of transfers would be required and that’s a nonstarter
children.textZhHtml: 您为什么认为它有效？假设您在达拉斯有一个 100 人的社区。该社区将向各个方向通勤，当然您可能能够运送一些朝同一方向行驶的团体，但完全缺乏中央办公室，那么最后一英里如何运作呢？需要进行大量的转账，这是不可能的

children.author: hahla
children.textRawHtml: Your entire view point is framed incorrectly. The problem isn’t can a bus solve the problem, it’s the majority of people don’t want to endure the hassle of riding the bus.
children.textZhHtml: 您的整个观点的框架不正确。问题不是公交车能解决问题，而是大多数人不愿意忍受坐公交车的麻烦。

children.author: ricardobayes
children.textRawHtml: Not saying to refute your point just flagging that in places like Germany the bus works flawlessly. People there are really proud that you can even go hiking with public transport, buses are clean, safe and cheap (cheaper than using your car).
children.textZhHtml: 并不是说要反驳你的观点，只是指出在德国等地，公交车运行得非常完美。那里的人们真的很自豪，你甚至可以乘坐公共交通工具去徒步旅行，公共汽车干净、安全、便宜（比开车便宜）。
